name: Nicholas Stern
industryTies: HSBC Centre for Climate Change and Sustainability
description: Nicholas Stern authored the landmark 2006 Stern Review on the Economics of Climate Change for the UK government, the first major government-commissioned economic analysis to argue that the benefits of early climate action vastly outweigh the costs — a conclusion that shifted the entire framing of climate policy from sacrifice narrative to economic opportunity. His work on discount rates for long-horizon risks catalyzed a decade of academic debate between environmental economists and continues to anchor IPCC Working Group III assessments. Stern holds the I.G. Patel Chair at LSE's Grantham Research Institute and is a Fellow of the British Academy and the Royal Society. He advises multiple sovereign wealth funds and development banks on green transition finance and was awarded a life peerage as Baron Stern of Brentford in 2007. His recent research focuses on the economics of biodiversity loss as a systemic financial risk comparable to climate.
